Strong fits include: wildfire detection tech and BC Wildfire monitoring systems, satellite/drone surveillance for Chilcotin wilderness, wildlife tracking and conservation technology, watershed sensors and salmon habitat monitoring, weather stations and climate tracking in backcountry, avalanche forecasting tech, trail mapping and GPS systems, outdoor recreation apps and connectivity, backcountry communication devices (satellite messengers, Meshtastic), flood/drought prediction systems, remote cameras for wildlife research, and how technology helps manage and protect Cariboo wild spaces. Prefer articles that bridge wilderness/conservation AND technology. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): prehistoric and ancient biology (fossils, palaeontology, deep-time creatures) with no contemporary conservation technology angle — these belong to Sunday's Science theme; AI and data centre infrastructure stories about business strategy, investment, or corporate politics rather than direct wilderness, ecosystem, or land-use impact in BC; geopolitical conflict, war, and crime news with no outdoor or conservation relevance; consumer tech reviews and financial market stories; general political and judicial news. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

items.content_html:

The slowdown could eventually reshape weather patterns, rainfall, storms, winters, and coastal sea levels around the Atlantic.

items.title: [phys.org] Fire amoeba breaks complex-life heat tolerance record at 63°C
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Scientists have identified a new amoeba, Incendiamoeba cascadensis, that can eat, move and reproduce in water as hot as 63°C (145°F) at California’s Lassen Volcanic National Park, setting a record for the highest temperature known to support eukaryotic reproduction. The NASA-supported study, published in Cell on Sept. 22, found that the organism remains active at about 64°C and can recover after five minutes at 70°C, although exposure to 80°C proved fatal [phys.org#1][nasa.gov#1][livescience.com#1][sciencenews.org#1]. The finding challenges the previous 60°C upper limit for eukaryotic growth and reproduction, based on the heat sensitivity of proteins and other complex cellular structures. Researchers said the amoeba withstands the heat by changing shape and forming a protective outer layer; genetic analysis also identified genes associated with repairing heat-damaged proteins [nasa.gov#1][science.org#1][orf.at#1]. The work is relevant to astrobiology because scientists use extreme environments on Earth to assess where complex life might survive on Mars and other worlds [nasa.gov#1][npr.org#1].

items.content_html:

The Arctic sea ice melt season is roughly 40 days longer than it was in 1979, yet its rapid expansion unexpectedly leveled off around 2010. Scientists say changing clouds and increasingly thin ice may explain the pause, but continued Arctic warming could eventually trigger another period of rapid change.

items.content_html:

Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone may have been carried from Scotland to Dogger Bank by glaciers before prehistoric people transported it hundreds of kilometers to Salisbury Plain. The possible multistage journey suggests remarkable organization and raises the possibility that the stone was valued long before it became part of Stonehenge.
